member.name: T:MajSimai.Parsing.ChartScanner
member.summary: The first pass over a chart text: reads BPM, beat, speed and signature changes, creates the comma timing points, and collects the note text of every timing point without reading the notes yet.

list.item: Lines and columns start from 1; the column of a timing point is the column of its comma.
|| starts a comment that runs to the end of its line. ||s3/4 also sets the time signature.
(bpm), {beats} and <HS*x> / <SV*x> declarations must be closed; a declaration that is not closed throws in every mode.
An E at the start of note text ends the chart unless the next character that is not whitespace is a digit: whitespace and line breaks are skipped as everywhere in simai, so E\n3 is the sensor E3.
In lenient mode, note text cut off by ( or {, note text without a comma at the end, and stray characters are dropped; strict mode throws for them.

member.summary: Reads the notes of one timing point into values.

remarks.para: The text of a timing point is split by / into notes; a note with * is a same head group whose later parts start from the button of the first part. Two digits such as 18 are two taps.

In lenient mode these notes are skipped and logged as warnings: a note with nothing left after removing its markers, a touch area letter that is not at the start of a note, a duration with too many separators or with text between the two # of [wait##length], and a hold whose ] comes before its [. Empty * parts are skipped too. A note that cannot be read is skipped as well, as are empty / parts, an unreadable hold duration becomes 0, and a b or m in the middle of a slide path is ignored; these are logged at the debug level.
Strict mode throws for all of these, and also checks the shape of taps, holds and touches and the path of slides (see ).

One thread parses about 20,000 characters per millisecond, so a shorter file is done before other threads would help.
